primary_sources.title: Introduction to Linear Algebra, Chapter 10.1: Graphs and Networks
primary_sources.author: Gilbert Strang
primary_sources.exact_anchor: pp. 452-454, especially equation (1) and the discussion immediately after it: the incidence matrix sends node potentials to edge differences; loop sums characterize its column space; connected nullspace potentials are constant.
primary_sources.supports: The conventional incidence-matrix, potential-difference, spanning-tree, and additive-constant framing used for the block-null theorem and its two-anchor extinction.
primary_sources.does_not_support: The source-specific channel word, carry recurrence, exponential error bound, or Erdos 269 application.

primary_sources.exact_anchor: Introduction and Section 2: edge potentials on connected graphs are organized by graph cohomology, with synchronizability/trivial holonomy corresponding to consistency of vertex-potential data.
primary_sources.supports: Modern standard use of potential, coboundary/cohomology, and consistency language for finite graph edge data.
primary_sources.does_not_support: Novelty for the elementary additive three-state specialization or any carry-lift conclusion.

mechanism_comparison.standard_core: A path increment with return sums zero depends only on endpoint states and is an exact one-cochain; zero differences on a spanning tree force the potential constant.
mechanism_comparison.local_delta: The exact Erdos 269 lift algebra turns vanishing perturbation into multiplicative error growth and proves that unit-accurate canonical representatives fail the first complete block.
mechanism_comparison.weighted_boundary: The actual recurrence telescopes to endpoint errors plus a weighted interior sum. That identity does not imply the ordinary unweighted block-null premise.
mechanism_comparison.significance_boundary: This is a proof-strategy no-go and semantic correction, not evidence that the target series is irrational.

observatory_adjudication_2026_08_26.comparison_relation: The abstract return-block statement is the standard exact-potential/graph-coboundary characterization on a finite state word; the carry-lift extinction and first-block witness are a source-specific conditional composition. The actual recurrence has weighted interior terms, so the premise is not established for the genuine orbit.
observatory_adjudication_2026_08_26.closest_known_result: Incidence-matrix potential differences, spanning-tree grounding, and exact one-cochain language are standard in Strang and in modern synchronization/cohomology treatments. No primary source located for this exact three-channel carry composition or its first-block arithmetic witness.
observatory_adjudication_2026_08_26.exact_delta: The local Lean package proves that ordinary block-nullity plus two anchor transitions forces the three-state perturbation to vanish; radix-product propagation then rules out bounded nonzero error, and unit-accurate canonical representatives fail the first complete block. It also exposes the weighted/unweighted premise gap.
observatory_adjudication_2026_08_26.disconfirming_evidence: The clean coboundary theorem does not apply unless ordinary return sums vanish; the actual weighted recurrence supplies a different block-defect identity. Thus the result cannot exclude weighted lifts, integral tails, or #269 itself.
